Bill number: HB1163
<bill_text>
SENATE BILL 1019
 By White

 HOUSE BILL 1163

 By Stevens

 AN ACT to amend Chapter __ of the Public Acts of 2025
 (1st Ex. Sess. – SB 6001 / HB 6004); and
 Tennessee Code Annotated, Title 49, Chapter 13
 and Title 49, Chapter 3, relative to education
 funding for public charter schools.

BE IT ENACTED BY THE GENERAL ASSEMBLY OF THE STATE OF TENNESSEE:

 SECTION 1. Tennessee Code Annotated, Section 49-3-103(d)(3), is amended by

adding the language "or public charter school" after the language "Explain how an LEA".

 SECTION 2. Tennessee Code Annotated, Section 49-3-105, is amended by deleting

subsection (d) and substituting instead the following:

 (d)

 (1) The funding that a student generates pursuant to this section must be

 administered and allocated by the department to the LEA in which the student is

 a member for the duration of the student's membership in the LEA, except that:

 (A) The funding a student generates pursuant to subdivision

 (c)(3) must not be allocated to the LEA, but must be maintained by the

 department; and

 (B) The state share of the funding a public charter school student

 generates for an LEA pursuant to this section must not be allocated to the

 LEA, but must be allocated directly to the public charter school.

 (2) A student's membership in an LEA begins on the first day of the

 student's membership and ends on the last day of the student's membership in

 the LEA, except that the membership of a student who graduates early is

 extended to the student's expected graduation date for funding purposes.

 SECTION 3. Tennessee Code Annotated, Section 49-3-316, is amended by adding the

language "or public charter school" after the language "LEA" wherever it appears in subsection

(c) and by adding the following as a new subsection:

 (f)

 (1) The commissioner, in consultation with the comptroller of the

 treasury, shall develop, revise as necessary, and prescribe a standardized

 system of financial accounting and reporting for all public charter schools,

 including appropriate forms or other documentation. This system must be

 designed to facilitate year-to-year and agency-to-agency comparison, as well as

 adequately indicating the sources and uses of all funds received by each public

 charter school. The commissioner shall review the fiscal public school records in

 all public charter schools to the end that the expenditure of funds, whether for

 current operation and maintenance purposes, capital outlay purposes, and other

 school purposes, are properly accounted for and safeguarded.

 (2) The commissioner may require public charter schools that receive

 allocations of state education funding pursuant to part 1 of this chapter or

 otherwise to comply with one (1) or more of the requirements established for

 LEAs in this section, as the commissioner deems appropriate or applicable.

 SECTION 4. Tennessee Code Annotated, Section 49-13-112, is amended by deleting

subsection (a) and substituting instead the following:

 (a)

 (1) A local board of education shall allocate to the public charter school

 an amount equal to:

 (A) The local student-generated funds for member students in the

 public charter school for the prior year in alignment with the TISA

 pursuant to chapter 3, part 1 of this title;

 (B) The average per pupil state and local funds received by the

 district in the current school year above those required by the TISA for

 each member student in the public charter school in the prior year;

 (C) The per student state and local funds received by the LEA for

 member students in the public charter school in the current school year

 beyond the prior year's membership; and

 (D) All appropriate allocations under federal law or regulation,

 including, but not limited to, IDEA and ESEA funds.

 (2) The department of education shall allocate directly to the public

charter school an amount equal to the state student-generated funds for member

students in the public charter school for the prior year in alignment with the TISA

pursuant to chapter 3, part 1 of this title.

 (3) Federal funds received by the LEA must be disbursed to public

charter schools authorized by the LEA by either joint agreement on shared

services by individual public charter schools or sub-grants to a public charter

school for the public charter school's equitable share of the federal grant based

on eligible students. The allocation must be made in accordance with the

policies and procedures developed by the department of education.

 (4) Each LEA shall include as part of its budget submitted pursuant to §

49-2-203, the per pupil amount of local money it will pass through to public

charter schools during the upcoming school year, including all calculations listed

in this section. Allocations to public charter schools during that year must be

 based on the calculated amounts. The LEA shall distribute the portion of local

 funds it expects to receive in no fewer than nine (9) equal installments to public

 charter schools in the same manner as state funds are distributed pursuant to

 chapter 3 of this title. An LEA shall adjust local payments to public charter

 schools, at a minimum, in October, February, and June, based on changes in

 revenue, student membership, or student services. All funds received by a public

 charter school must be spent according to the budget submitted or as otherwise

 revised by the public charter school governing body, subject to the requirements

 of state and federal law.

 SECTION 5. Sections 1 and 3 of this act take effect upon becoming a law, the public

welfare requiring it. For rulemaking purposes, Sections 2 and 4 of this act take effect upon

becoming a law, the public welfare requiring it. For all other purposes, Sections 2 and 4 of this

act take effect July 1, 2025, the public welfare requiring it.
</bill_text>

<summary>
This bill would change how public charter schools are funded and tracked under Tennessee's education funding law, which the text refers to as the TISA. It would send the state share of funding for charter school students directly to the charter school instead of to the local school system (LEA).

Section 1 would add "or public charter school" to a provision in Section 49-3-103(d)(3) that begins "Explain how an LEA." The text does not show what the provision requires.

Section 2 would replace Section 49-3-105(d). Funding a student generates would go through the state department of education to the LEA where the student is a member, for as long as the student is a member. There are two exceptions. Funding generated under subdivision (c)(3) would stay with the department. The state share of funding that a charter school student generates would go straight to the charter school. Membership would start on the student's first day and end on the last day. A student who graduates early would count as a member until the expected graduation date for funding purposes.

Section 3 would add "or public charter school" after "LEA" in Section 49-3-316(c). It would also add a new subsection (f). The commissioner of education, with the comptroller, would set up a standard financial accounting and reporting system for all charter schools. It would be designed to allow comparisons across years and agencies and to show the sources and uses of all funds. The commissioner would review charter school fiscal records to make sure spending is properly accounted for and safeguarded. The commissioner could also require charter schools that receive state education funding to follow one or more of the requirements that apply to LEAs in that section, as the commissioner considers appropriate.

Section 4 would replace Section 49-13-112(a). A local board of education would have to give each charter school an amount equal to four items. The first is the local student-generated funds for its member students for the prior year. The second is the average per-pupil state and local funds above those the TISA requires. The third is the per-student state and local funds received for members beyond the prior year's membership. The fourth is all appropriate federal allocations, including IDEA and ESEA funds. The department of education would pay charter schools directly the state student-generated funds for the prior year. Federal funds the LEA receives would go to charter schools through joint agreements for shared services or through sub-grants for an equitable share, following department policies. Each LEA would list in its budget the per-pupil local amount it will pass to charter schools, with its calculations. It would pay the local funds in at least nine equal installments, the same way state funds are paid. It would adjust payments at least in October, February, and June to reflect changes in revenue, membership, or services. Charter schools must spend funds according to their budget, or as their governing body revises it, subject to state and federal law.

Sections 1 and 3 would take effect when the bill becomes law. Sections 2 and 4 would also take effect then for rulemaking. For all other purposes, they would take effect July 1, 2025.
</summary>

There are two exceptions. Funding generated under subdivision (c)(3) would stay with the department. assessments.rationale: Covers the department's allocation role, membership-based duration, and both exceptions.

assessments.summary_quote: Membership would start on the student's first day and end on the last day. A student who graduates early would count as a member until the expected graduation date for funding purposes.
assessments.rationale: States the membership period and the early-graduation funding exception.

assessments.summary_quote: Section 3 would add "or public charter school" after "LEA" in Section 49-3-316(c).
assessments.rationale: Identifies the target subsection and conveys the extension of its LEA references to public charter schools.

assessments.summary_quote: The commissioner of education, with the comptroller, would set up a standard financial accounting and reporting system for all charter schools. It would be designed to allow comparisons across years and agencies and to show the sources and uses of all funds.
assessments.rationale: Covers the responsible officials, system scope, and design objectives, but omits revision as necessary and the required forms or documentation.

assessments.summary_quote: The commissioner would review charter school fiscal records to make sure spending is properly accounted for and safeguarded.
assessments.rationale: Conveys the mandatory review and its accounting and safeguarding purposes; the general reference to spending encompasses the listed expenditure categories.

assessments.summary_quote: The commissioner could also require charter schools that receive state education funding to follow one or more of the requirements that apply to LEAs in that section, as the commissioner considers appropriate.
assessments.rationale: Covers the commissioner's discretion, eligible charter schools, and application of LEA requirements from the identified section.

assessments.summary_quote: Section 4 would replace Section 49-13-112(a). A local board of education would have to give each charter school an amount equal to four items. The first is the local student-generated funds for its member students for the prior year.
assessments.rationale: Identifies the obligated board, recipient, local student-generated funding amount, and prior-year membership basis within the summary's TISA funding context.

assessments.summary_quote: The second is the average per-pupil state and local funds above those the TISA requires.
assessments.rationale: Identifies above-TISA state and local funding, but omits that the district receives it in the current year and that allocation is for each prior-year charter member student.

assessments.summary_quote: The third is the per-student state and local funds received for members beyond the prior year's membership.
assessments.rationale: Conveys funding for membership growth, but does not specify current-year charter membership or that the funds are received by the LEA.

assessments.summary_quote: The fourth is all appropriate federal allocations, including IDEA and ESEA funds.
assessments.rationale: Within the list of required local-board allocations, covers appropriate federal funding and both named programs.

assessments.summary_quote: The department of education would pay charter schools directly the state student-generated funds for the prior year.
assessments.rationale: Conveys direct departmental payment of the prior-year state student-generated amount; the surrounding discussion supplies the charter-member and TISA context.

assessments.summary_quote: Federal funds the LEA receives would go to charter schools through joint agreements for shared services or through sub-grants for an equitable share, following department policies.
assessments.rationale: Covers both disbursement methods and departmental policies, but omits the limitation to LEA-authorized charter schools and the eligible-student basis for equitable shares.

assessments.summary_quote: Each LEA would list in its budget the per-pupil local amount it will pass to charter schools, with its calculations.
assessments.rationale: Covers budget disclosure, but omits the upcoming-school-year timeframe and the requirement that actual allocations be based on those calculated amounts.

assessments.summary_quote: It would pay the local funds in at least nine equal installments, the same way state funds are paid.
assessments.rationale: In context, identifies the LEA's local-fund payments to charter schools and preserves the minimum installment count, equality, and distribution manner.

assessments.summary_quote: It would adjust payments at least in October, February, and June to reflect changes in revenue, membership, or services.
assessments.rationale: Covers the LEA's local-payment adjustments, all required months, and all adjustment grounds.

assessments.summary_quote: Charter schools must spend funds according to their budget, or as their governing body revises it, subject to state and federal law.
assessments.rationale: Conveys the budget-based spending requirement, governing-body revision authority, and state and federal legal constraints.
